item.description: - Numbers → Prefer digits now covers spoken times ("ten thirty" → 10:30), years ("twenty twenty five" → 2025), phone-number digit runs, "a hundred people" → 100 people, "fifteen hundred" → 1500, and date ordinals ("the twenty-first of October" → the 21st of October). Smart is unchanged. - Live dictation captions expand correctly instead of appearing cropped inside a small black box. Larger text also keeps the Stop and Cancel buttons visible. - Dictionary sound-alike matching catches more split brand names, such as "ads viser" for "Adzviser". Taught spellings also tolerate spacing changes. - Add dictionary words in bulk: paste a list or two spreadsheet columns, review the spellings and optional mishearings, and save them together. Existing corrections are kept and duplicate entries are skipped.
- The dictation bubble stays near the mouse when an app reports an invalid text cursor location, instead of appearing at a screen corner.

- The dictation bubble opens at its final size instead of flashing a wide empty bar. Cursor placement settles before it appears, so a slow caret lookup no longer makes it jump across the screen. - Saying "period" at the end of a sentence now ends it, even without a pause: "I had salmon for dinner period" types "I had salmon for dinner." instead of "dinner, period." Phrases like "billing period" or "the Jurassic period" keep the word.
